text:
Krichene and Rendle’s [On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) shows sampled ranking metrics can reverse model orderings relative to full-catalog evaluation. Thus, describe results explicitly as HR@10 against 99 fixed negatives; retain the host evaluator and avoid claiming full-catalog improvements. Cawley and Talbot’s [model-selection study](https://jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html) explains how repeatedly maximizing a noisy validation score creates selection bias, including through checkpoint selection.

Recommended comparison: retain each model’s binary hit for every validation user. Bootstrap 200 users with replacement independently within each category, using identical resampled indices for both models; compute each category’s mean paired difference, then average the four differences equally. Report observed category/macro HR@10, macro improvement in percentage points, and a 95% percentile interval from, for example, 10,000 replicates with a disclosed bootstrap seed. User-based paired comparisons align with [offline recommendation evaluation research](https://castells.github.io/papers/irj2020.pdf). These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fitted models and fixed candidates; they exclude training-seed and negative-sampling variability and do not correct adaptive selection bias. Label comparisons selected after search exploratory.

Predeclare checkpoint evaluation cadence, stopping rule, tie-breaking, and maximum selection opportunities; report actual validation queries, checkpoints considered, and selected epochs. Optionally report each checkpoint’s bootstrap selection frequency as stability, not probability of superiority. For compute-matched ablations, allocate equal aggregate GPU-seconds and comparable selection opportunities, changing one component at a time. Report hardware, epochs/updates reached, completed/failed trials, and all charged training/diagnostic/debugging costs within 43,200 GPU-seconds; four concurrent slots do not multiply that budget. Disclose preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42; claim no across-seed robustness. Keep held-out testing exclusively for the host’s final evaluation.
